entry.title: Books to read if you're thinking of studying English at Oxford

media:group.media:title: Books to read if you're thinking of studying English at Oxford
media:group.media:description:
Thinking of studying English at Oxford? 📚
From literary theory to poetry, fiction and theatre, here are five books to get you thinking about how we study literature.
Please note: This isn't an official reading list, just some suggested reads by Magdalen College to explore, question and put into practice alongside the books you already love.
The books: 1. Introduction to Literature, Criticism, and Theory by Andrew Bennett and Nicholas Royle
Try to use the concepts you find here with the books you’ve already read, what do they make you think about?
2. Terry Eagleton, How to Read a Poem
This witty and very accessible book on poetry talks about how reading poetry might just be a skill we’re losing. The book goes through close analyses of poems from the renaissance to the present day, and is an excellent guide in your next steps of reading.
3. Key Concepts in Literary Theory, Julian Wolfreys, Ruth Robbins, and Kenneth Womack
Gives a broad range of concise definitions of the most significant terms used in literary theory today.
4. How Fiction Works by James Wood
A text looking at narrative, detail, characterisation, dialogue, realism, and style. Looking at a huge range of fiction from Beatrix Potter to John le Carré.
5. The Empty Space by Peter Brook - groundbreaking director Peter Brook covers important developments and breakthroughs in the theatre of the last century.
Read widely, read what excites you, and think deeply about it as you go.
🎬 | Magdalen College (First published June, 2026)

entry.title: How did Africa become a symbol of freedom?

media:group.media:title: How did Africa become a symbol of freedom?
media:group.media:description:
How did Africa’s image become a symbol of freedom, solidarity and unity?
As part of #BlackHistoryMonth, Karrington Harp shares her key takeaways from Oxford’s Black History Month Lecture 2026, The Iconicity of Africa, delivered by Professor Adom Getachew.
The lecture explored the history and enduring influence of Pan-Africanism and was organised by Oxford’s BME Staff Network in partnership with Nuffield College and the University's Equality and Diversity Unit.

entry.title: Oxford researcher reveals the psychology behind The Traitors with a former Faithful

media:group.media:title: Oxford researcher reveals the psychology behind The Traitors with a former Faithful
media:group.media:description:
'The biggest mistake is not making bad judgements; it’s believing them to be correct.'
As we head towards the final of The Celebrity Traitors, DPhil student Isaac Winterburn from Oxford's Department of Experimental Psychology explores the game's psychology, from confirmation bias to why we're not as good at spotting liars as we think.
Joining him is psychologist and former Faithful Dr Ellie Buckley, who shares her insights from inside the castle.
With thanks to Dr Ellie Buckley and the Oxford Psychology Society for their contributions to this video.
#TheTraitors #Psychology #OxfordUniversity
